name: LN2 cold-shock test of cryogenic ground-support components (pipe spools, valves, filters, flex hoses): fill with LN2 until it exits, then cold-soak for at least 1 h (KSC-STD-Z-0009 Rev D 6.2.1)
plain_name: Flood a cryogenic pipe section or valve with liquid nitrogen for an hour to prove it neither deforms nor leaks
description: After shop fabrication, cryogenic ground-support assemblies are cold-shock tested by introducing LN2 at the inlet until a steady LN2 stream exits, then maintaining the supply for a cold soak of at least 1 h; no deformation, leakage, frost or condensation on vacuum jackets is allowed, and annulus pressure is monitored until the assembly returns to ambient.
keywords: Flood a cryogenic pipe section or valve with liquid nitrogen for an hour to prove it neither deforms nor leaks

sources.citation: KSC-STD-Z-0009 Revision D, Design of Cryogenic Ground Systems and Ground Support Equipment, Standard for (NASA Kennedy Space Center)
Cryogenic Machining of Ti-6Al-4V (S. Isakson, Licentiate thesis, Chalmers University of Technology, 2018, report IMS-2018-12) (LN2 boiling point reference)

requirements.rationale: The test medium is liquid nitrogen fed continuously into the component.
The LN2 supply must be maintained for a cold soak of at least 1 hour.
Reference: LN2 at ambient pressure boils at -196 C, the temperature the component reaches during the soak.

confirmation_note: Requirements taken from the cited procedure and independently re-verified against the source (research/v4, 2026-11-01). Users must confirm them for their own run; edits require confirmation again.
